custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create a custom role for this test, role B, with Part Library & Inventory — View, Part Library & Inventory — Create & Edit and See Financial Data but without Part Library & Inventory — Delete, so user B can create and edit parts but cannot delete them.
  • Create a staff member for this test, user B, at the test location with role B, so the steps run with role B's permissions.
  • Use two browser windows: window 1 signed in as the Admin, window 2 (a private window) signed in as user B, so both users' screens can be seen side by side.
  • Create an active, tracked part, part A, for this test.
  • Start window 1 on role B's Edit Role page (Roles & Permissions), with nothing changed yet.
  • Start window 2 on the Inventory page, on the Active tab, with part A's part number typed in the Search box.

How to set this up on the QA site (https://sv10647.qa.shopview.com):

  • Admin at the test location: on the QA site's sign-in screen choose Admin. The test location is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919; its name shows in the box at the top right. If another name shows, click that box, click the name beside Change Location: and pick Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • To create a part: click Parts in the top bar, Inventory in the left menu, then New Inventory Part. Fill Description and Part Number (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C425647-A for part A, -B for part B), pick a Category, type a Cost and a Sell Price, type the Quantity in the bin row (the location's bin, for example General Storage, is offered), then click Save. Leave Track quantities and cost of goods on for a tracked part; click it off for an untracked part. Add Bin Location adds a second bin; Vendor, Manufacturer, Core Charge, Min, Max and Tags are in the same window. Parts that must start with the same text all start ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C425647-, so searching for that finds them all.
  • The Search box above the Inventory list opens when you click Search (the magnifier).
  • Settings: click the box at the top right, then Settings in its menu. The left menu then lists Staff, Roles & Permissions, Bin Locations and Categories, and Inventory under IMPORTS.
  • To create a custom role: Settings, then Roles & Permissions in the left menu, then Create Custom Role; in Choose a template click Skip; type the Role Name; switch on Parts Department, then tick the boxes the setup names on its three rows, Part sales, Part Library and Inventory, and Vendor and order management (each has View, Create & Edit and Delete); See Financial Data is under Cross-Cutting Toggles; then click Create. (The setup above writes these boxes as, for example, Part Library & Inventory — View, which is the View box on the Part Library and Inventory row.)
  • User B: the QA site's sign-in screen offers only Admin and Tech, so user B is the shared Tech sign-in given role B for this test. Signed in as Admin: Settings, then Staff in the left menu; click Search, type tech@shopview.com, click the edit icon at the end of Tech ShopView's row, pick role B under Role and click Save & Close. Then, in the second (private) window, choose Tech on the sign-in screen. When the test is finished, set Tech ShopView's Role back to Technician the same way, because other testers use that sign-in.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens for part A: Part Status shows Active and Inactive, both greyed out, so user B cannot pick them.

Step 2:

  • The window closes.

Step 3:

  • The Delete box is ticked.

Step 4:

  • Role B is saved.

Step 5:

  • The Inventory page reloads for user B.

Step 6:

  • The menu now lists Cycle count, Deactivate parts and Export: the role has exactly what was granted.

Step 7:

  • The menu closes.

Step 8:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens for part A, with Part Status no longer greyed out.

Step 9:

  • Inactive is picked.

Step 10:

  • The "Deactivate part?" confirmation opens.

Step 11:

  • A green message reads "Part deactivated." and part A leaves the Active tab.

Step 12:

  • The Inactive tab is selected.

Step 13:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens for part A.

Step 14:

  • Active is picked.

Step 15:

  • The "Activate part?" confirmation opens.

Step 16:

  • A green message reads "Part activated." and part A leaves the Inactive tab.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10821 (Story 8, Permissions), story SV-10826 (Story 13, The Part Dialog)

  • S8-R1: “Setting a part inactive requires the 'Part Library & Inventory → Delete' permission.”
  • S8-R2: “Setting a part active requires the same permission.”
  • S8-R16: “A custom role has only the permissions granted to it.”
  • S8-R6: “That user sees the Part Status choice in the part dialog disabled (S13-R20).”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Part deactivated from the part dialog | "Part deactivated." | Success toast, fades on its own”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Part activated from the part dialog | "Part activated." | Success toast, fades on its own”
